hospitals.description: Children's National is the freestanding children's hospital for the District and the main pediatric referral center for the whole Washington region, on a shared campus with MedStar Washington Hospital Center near Howard University. It runs a Level IV NICU that a neonatal directory lists at 54 beds, a PICU and cardiac ICU, a busy pediatric emergency department and trauma program, and essentially every pediatric subspecialty. Its neonatologists and hospitalists also staff partner NICUs and pediatric units across DC, suburban Maryland and Northern Virginia, so many regional NP roles are Children's National jobs. It is the academic pediatrics home for George Washington University and reportedly employs one of the largest pediatric APP workforces on the East Coast.
highlights: Freestanding children's hospital serving DC, Maryland and Virginia
Level IV NICU (54 beds per neonatologysolutions directory)
Runs a network of regional partner NICUs in DC, MD and VA
PICU, cardiac ICU and full subspecialty range
Academic pediatrics for George Washington University
hospitals.notes: Biggest single employer of acute care PNPs in the DC region (inpatient, ICU, ED and subspecialty roles). Regional partner sites (Shady Grove, GW, Howard, VHC, Reston, StoneSprings, Sentara NoVA, Stafford, Mary Washington, Cedar Hill) post under Children's National. Verify bed count, trauma level and Magnet status during enrichment.

hospitals.description: MedStar Georgetown is the teaching hospital of Georgetown University, set on the university's hilltop campus in northwest Washington. Its pediatric program centers on a 14-bed multidisciplinary PICU for patients up to age 22, supervised around the clock by pediatric intensivists and backed by a ground and air PICU transport service for the mid-Atlantic. The hospital also runs Georgetown's pediatric residency, general pediatric inpatient care and a pediatric transplant program through the MedStar Georgetown Transplant Institute. The neighborhood is residential Georgetown and Glover Park, with limited parking and most staff commuting by shuttle or bus.

hospitals.description: George Washington University Hospital is GW's academic medical center in Foggy Bottom, a few blocks from the White House and the Kennedy Center. It is a major adult trauma and tertiary center, and its pediatric footprint is the obstetric service and a Level III NICU run in partnership with Children's National neonatology. General pediatric inpatient care for GW is provided at Children's National rather than on this campus. The hospital sits on the Foggy Bottom Metro stop, which makes it one of the easiest DC hospitals to reach without a car.
highlights: GW's academic medical center in Foggy Bottom
Level III NICU staffed with Children's National neonatology
Adult Level I trauma center (reportedly)
On the Foggy Bottom Metro station
hospitals.notes: NICU Level III per the Children's National regional NICU page; NICU NP roles likely post under Children's National. No inpatient pediatric unit known on this campus. Careers URL is a guess at the UHS hospital careers path; enrichment should confirm.

hospitals.description: MedStar Washington Hospital Center is the largest private hospital in the District and the flagship of MedStar Health, sharing a campus with Children's National in the Brookland and Michigan Park corridor. It is the region's main adult trauma, cardiac and burn referral center and the base for MedSTAR air and ground transport. Pediatric patients on campus are mostly cared for next door at Children's National, but the hospital runs a large obstetric service with a newborn intensive care program. It trains residents with Georgetown and anchors a dense medical district reachable from the Brookland Metro.
highlights: Largest private hospital in Washington, DC
Shares a campus with Children's National
Regional adult trauma, cardiac and burn center (reportedly)
Base of the MedSTAR transport service
hospitals.notes: Included as an academic medical center. No inpatient pediatric unit known (Children's National is adjacent). A NICU is reportedly present; verify level. Expect few PNP postings; neonatal NP roles possible.

hospitals.description: Howard University Hospital is the teaching hospital of Howard University College of Medicine, a historically Black academic medical center on Georgia Avenue in the Shaw and Pleasant Plains area. It runs a Level III NICU and transitional nursery that expanded its partnership with Children's National in 2022, so Children's National neonatology now supports care there. Howard trains pediatric residents and serves a largely Black, lower-income patient base from Wards 1, 4, 5 and the surrounding neighborhoods. The campus is next to the Shaw-Howard University Metro station.
highlights: Teaching hospital of Howard University College of Medicine
Level III NICU with Children's National partnership (expanded 2022)
Historically Black academic medical center
Next to the Shaw-Howard University Metro
